_comment: Decides which jobs are worth an LLM scoring call, and in what order. See jobs/relevance.py. This is the ONLY file that knows this pipeline is currently pointed at software roles -- relevance.py itself contains no domain terms, so retargeting at a different field means rewriting this file and config/persona.json, not touching code.
_why: ingest/ats.py pulls entire company job boards, so ~87% of the table is roles this persona will never apply to (compliance, enterprise sales, clinical, tax). Scoring used to be the only filter, which meant paying an LLM call to conclude that a Chief Compliance Officer posting is not a software job.
_tiers: 1 = title matches and location is acceptable. 2 = title matches, location unknown or elsewhere. 3 = everything else. Nothing is ever deleted; max_tier_to_score just decides how deep today's budget reaches, so raising it backfills previously-skipped rows with no re-ingest.
_regex_dialect: These are POSTGRES regexes (~*), not Python ones. Word boundary is \y -- in Postgres \b means BACKSPACE, so a \b pattern silently matches nothing and quietly demotes everything it was meant to catch to tier 3. This was not hypothetical: the first version of this file used \b throughout and buried 'ML / LLM Engineer' and 'Senior / Staff Fullstack Engineer' in tier 3. Always re-run tools/relevance-report.py after editing.
_dead_patterns_note: tools/relevance-report.py --dead lists patterns matching zero rows. That report exists to catch \b-instead-of-\y mistakes, NOT to prune correct-but-currently-unused terms. '\yattorney\y' and '\ywarehouse\y' match nothing today and are kept on purpose: both were verified to match a synthetic title in Postgres, so they are working exclusions waiting for their first posting. Deleting an exclusion because the role has not appeared yet is how it appears in tier 1 next week.
_title_include_note: Deliberately wider than 'engineer'. The persona's strongest bucket (bridge_solutions) is customer-facing implementation work -- Forward Deployed Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Technical Account Manager -- which a narrow engineering regex would push to tier 3 and never score. Better to spend a few calls on near-misses than to silently lose the best-fit bucket.
_title_exclude_note: Narrow and specific on purpose. Broad words that merely CO-OCCUR with unwanted roles -- 'manager', 'lead', 'director', 'specialist' -- are absent deliberately: they also appear in Engineering Manager and Technical Lead. An over-eager exclude is worse than no exclude, because tier 3 is where things go to be forgotten. Exclude only what is unambiguous.
_company_exclude_note: Matched against company_name, not title. These six are relist sites that Google Jobs reports AS the employer, so the actual employer is unknown and an app would display the job board's name in the company field. 113 rows as of 2026-07-26. Their titles are keyword-stuffed in exactly the way title_include rewards, which is how 19 of them reached match_score >= 90 -- one at match 99 against an LLM fit of 15. Four of the six scrub the employer out of the body entirely (see description_exclude): remote zest 50/50, remote click 23/23, vacancy global 5/5, BrightHush 3/3.
_company_exclude_scope_note: Deliberately does NOT list bebee, jobleads, learn4good, whatjobs, jooble, lensa, theladders, dailyremote, salutemyjob, remotejobs.org or jobright.ai, even though 150+ job_url values point at them. For those rows company_name holds the REAL employer and only the apply link is routed through the aggregator -- annoying to click, but a genuine posting, and excluding by company_name would match zero of them anyway. Add a pattern here only after confirming the name actually appears in company_name.
_company_exclude_rejected_note: Rejected alternative: flag rows where SerpApi's `via` field matches company_name. It catches 160 rows but false-positives on every company posting to its own careers site -- via='Cisco Careers'/company='Cisco', 'Snowflake Careers'/'Snowflake', Capital One, Deloitte, ServiceNow, Citadel, D. E. Shaw. Those are the BEST rows in the table. Measured on all 632 Google rows, then rejected; do not revive it without re-running that check.
_description_exclude_note: Some relisters scrub the employer's name out of the body and substitute a placeholder, leaving text like 'reputed company is redefining IT operations for the modern reputed company'. 82 rows read that way. A posting whose employer has been deleted cannot be applied to no matter how good the title looks, and unlike company_exclude this catches the same spam when it arrives under a fresh company name. Keep this list tiny and literal -- it scans description_text, so a loose pattern here could bury thousands of legitimate rows.
_location_note: Any-of. These are heuristic tag columns set at ingest; NULL (source could not tell) reads as tier 2, not tier 3, so an undetectable location never buries a good posting. Set to [] to ignore location entirely.
_max_tier_note: 2 means tier-3 rows are not scored while the backlog is being worked through. Set to 3 to open the floodgates once throughput allows -- those rows are still sitting there, unscored, waiting.
